quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Yield to all traffic before crossing.
Stop, then enter when it is safe.
Slow down and cross carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down to a safe speed and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What should you do if the road ahead is covered with heavy smoke?

options.text: Turn on your flashers and continue.
Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the road.
Turn on your high beams and continue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: If you see heavy smoke ahead, slow down immediately, move as far right as possible, and stop off the road. Then check if it is safe to continue. Heavy smoke can harm your eyes and lungs.

questions.question: When should you move back into the right lane after passing?

options.text: When you are one vehicle length ahead of the other car.
When you can see both headlights of the other car in your mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other car in your mirror.
questions.explanation: You have enough space to return to the right lane when you can see both headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from behind, you should NOT:

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the headrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Keep your seat belt on. Brace yourself by pressing against the back of your seat and rest your head against the headrest to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:

options.text: Start to slow down.
Flash your headlights.
Give a sharp blast of your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give a sharp blast of your horn.
questions.explanation: Use a sharp horn blast to warn a child or pedestrian who is about to enter the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Leave the front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb. When parking uphill without a curb or parking downhill, turn wheels toward the curb or road edge.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Brake lightly.
Stay off the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes during a skid. Braking can make the skid worse.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light and have not yet entered. You should:

options.text: Speed up to get through before the light turns red.
Slow down and go through carefully.
Come to a safe stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a safe stop.
questions.explanation: Stop safely at a steady yellow light if you have not entered the intersection yet. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue at a safe speed.

questions.question: A pennant-shaped sign means:

options.text: No passing zone.
Right turn allowed on red.
Yield right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A pennant-shaped sign marks the start of a no passing zone.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should NOT:

options.text: Continue to find an alternate route.
Go to the next exit and find another way.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up on the road or shoulder. Continue to the next exit or crossroad. Other drivers will not expect you to back up and could hit you.

questions.question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must:

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
Stop only if you are going in the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus picks up or drops off passengers, regardless of which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: A dashed white line in the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Lanes travel in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Lanes travel in the same direction and passing is allowed.
Lanes travel in opposite directions and passing is allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes travel in the same direction and passing is allowed.
questions.explanation: A dashed white line means you can cross it to pass or change lanes. White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly enough to stop within your headlights' light.
Use high beam headlights to see better.
Keep dashboard lights bright so others can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough to stop within your headlights' light.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: What does this yellow warning sign mean?

options.text: A school or school crossing is ahead.
Slow down and watch for children.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers near schools. It means you should slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Stop sign ahead.
Divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn in the direction the arrow points. In this case, you cannot turn right.

questions.question: When leaving an alley or driveway to enter traffic, you should:

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
Expect pedestrians to yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the sidewalk from an alley or driveway. Pedestrians and traffic have the right-of-way.

questions.question: When is pavement most slippery?

options.text: After it has rained for several hours.
When rain just begins.
After it has rained for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain just begins.
questions.explanation: Pavement is most slippery at the start of rain. Dirt and oil mix with water, creating a slick surface.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection with vehicles arriving at the same time from your right and left, you should:

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until the intersection is clear before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Vehicles proceed in the order they arrived.

questions.question: When parking uphill with no curb, you should set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn wheels toward the edge of the road.
Turn wheels away from the edge of the road.
Keep wheels facing straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn wheels toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Turn your front wheels right toward the road edge. If the brakes fail, the car will roll off the road instead of into traffic.

questions.question: To stay safe from an airbag, sit ____ inches from the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Sit 10 inches from the steering wheel center to your chest. This distance gives you protection if the airbag deploys in a crash.

questions.question: You are in the left lane with two lanes going your direction. Many vehicles pass you on the right. You should:

options.text: Stay in your lane to not block traffic.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let vehicles pass.
Move to the right lane when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane for passing or turning left. Use the right lane when driving slower than traffic or when turning right.

questions.question: You reach a four-way stop at the same time as the driver on your left. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left.
You do.
Whoever signals a turn first.

questions.correctAnswerText: You do.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop with vehicles arriving at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. The driver on your left is to your left, so you have the right-of-way.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will make room for you.
Assume the driver will let you pass if you signal.
Assume the driver will drive at a constant speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will make room for you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will move or give you space to pass, even with a signal. Check that it is safe before you pass.

questions.question: A broken yellow centerline means:

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when safe.
You can pass on the left when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when safe.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can cross it to pass. You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.

questions.question: You have a green light but traffic blocks the intersection ahead. You should:

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Wait outside the intersection until traffic clears.
Enter the intersection with other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait outside the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if traffic blocks your path, even if the light is green. Entering will block traffic when the light changes. You can get a ticket for blocking an intersection.
